title: Call-end "Ciao" goodbye sound
summary: A warm, slightly-long, stressed spoken "Ciao" is played to a participant when they LEAVE a call. Applies to BOTH voice and video calls. In 1:1 calls, when either person ends the call BOTH participants hear the Ciao (the call ends for both). In group calls, a participant hears it only after THEY leave the call (remaining members do not hear it).

behavior.trigger: Play the goodbye sound when the LOCAL participant's call transitions from connected/active to ended (they hung up, or the call ended for them).
behavior.oneToOne: Both sides transition to ended when either hangs up, so both devices play the Ciao once.
behavior.group: Only the participant who leaves transitions to ended locally, so only the leaver plays it. Remaining participants keep the call and play nothing.
doNotPlayOn: an unanswered outgoing call that is cancelled before it was ever connected
an incoming call that is declined/missed before being answered
a remote participant leaving a group call (only the person leaving hears it)

audioAsset.description: The web app synthesizes the Ciao once via text-to-speech and caches it in Convex File Storage; every web client reuses the cached URL.

web.queryReturns: string | null (a temporary Convex storage URL for the MP3, or null until generated)

native.recommendation: The native Android app should ship its OWN bundled short 'Ciao' sound asset (mp3/ogg in res/raw) and play it locally on call leave. Do NOT depend on the web Convex storage URL; it is a temporary signed URL intended for the web client. If you prefer a shared asset, request a permanent Hercules CDN URL from the web team.
native.delivery: Play the goodbye tone from the local FCM/Stream call-leave handler on the device, mirroring the trigger rules above.

notes: This is purely a client-side sound-effect feature; no change to the ringing path (notifyIncomingCall) or to any call orchestration mutation.
The web trigger keys off the local call status transition active -> ended in the CallProvider, which is why 1:1 plays for both and group plays only for the leaver.

mapping.trigger active->ended: hangup() runs on local End; the CallUI auto-end effect calls onHangup() when convStatus flips to ended/declined OR the remote drops (remoteParticipants.length===0), i.e. when the LOCAL call transitions to ended.
mapping.oneToOne both play: The non-initiator's CallUI detects the remote leaving + convStatus 'ended' and calls onHangup() -> hangup() -> plays. The initiator plays directly in hangup().
mapping.group leaver only: The auto-end effect early-returns while remoteParticipants.length > 0, so remaining group members never call hangup() and stay silent; only the leaver's hangup() plays.
mapping.doNotPlayOn unanswered/declined: playCallEndTone() is gated on remoteConnected (true only after a real connect); decline uses a separate path that never plays the tone.
mapping.bundled native asset: res/raw/incallmanager_busytone.(mp3) played via the custom native playInCallSound().

_nativeImplementationStatus.openIssue: Audibility during the live WebRTC/Stream audio session is still under diagnosis via on-device TONE Diagnostic Logs (see PRD iter-442/444).
